pl-l4d39c5-d1e115.summary: Asks whether, if a believer dismisses an unbeliever or the unbeliever departs, the believer may marry another.

pl-l4d39c5-d1e118.summary: Notes that authority seems to testify that he cannot marry another while she lives.

pl-l4d39c5-d1e121.summary: Quotes Ambrose: if you depart from each other and dismiss those willing to cohabit and join others, you are adulterers, and your children from that union are unclean, that is, illegitimate.
claims: Dismissing a willing spouse and remarrying is adultery.

pl-l4d39c5-d1e131.summary: Adds: one who had a virgin wife before baptism cannot have another while she lives after baptism, since crimes, not marriages, are dissolved in baptism.

pl-l4d39c5-d1e137.summary: Quotes Ambrose to the contrary: if the unbeliever departs, let him depart; the brother or sister is not bound, since the reverence of marriage is not owed to one who abhors the author of marriage; marriage without devotion to God is not ratified, so one dismissed for God's sake does not sin by remarrying; the insult to the Creator dissolves the right of marriage for the one left; the departing unbeliever sins against God and marriage. If both believe, marriage is confirmed by knowledge of God.
claims: One deserted by an unbeliever for the faith may remarry.
Insult to the Creator dissolves the marriage right.

pl-l4d39c5-d1e155.summary: Reconciles: dismissing a spouse willing to cohabit differs from being dismissed for God's sake by one who abhors Christ's name; one may dismiss a willing spouse but not remarry while she lives; one need not follow a departing spouse and may remarry. This applies only to those joined in unbelief; if both converted, or both married as believers, and one later abandons the faith and leaves the spouse from hatred of the faith, the deserted spouse may not remarry while the other lives, since their marriage was ratified and cannot be dissolved.
claims: Desertion for the faith allows remarriage; voluntary dismissal does not.
A ratified marriage between believers remains even after apostasy.

pl-l4d39c5.summary: Asks whether, if a believer dismisses or is left by an unbeliever, the believer may marry another. Ambrose seems to say no in one place, that remarrying is adultery and crimes, not marriages, are dissolved in baptism, but in another says that if the unbeliever departs, the believer is not bound and may remarry, since contempt of the Creator dissolves the right of marriage. Lombard distinguishes: dismissing a spouse willing to cohabit does not permit remarriage; being left for God's sake by one who hates Christ's name does. This concerns those married in unbelief; if both were believers and one apostatizes, the marriage was ratified and the deserted spouse cannot remarry.
claims: One who dismisses a peaceable unbelieving spouse cannot remarry.
One deserted for the faith by an unbelieving spouse may remarry.
This applies only to marriages contracted in unbelief.
A ratified marriage between believers is not dissolved by apostasy.
